reconcile.note: Henry argues that naming just one man isn't a denial of the second, since Mark never says there was only one.

discrepancy.note: Strauss says Matthew's two demoniacs versus Mark and Luke's one is a genuine narrative difference that harmonists have struggled to reconcile.

quotes.text: meets, according to Mark and Luke, a demoniac who lived among the tombs, … and was subject to outbreaks of terrific fury against himself … and others; according to Matthew, there were two. … It is astonishing how long harmonists have resorted to miserable expedients
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), on the Gadarene demoniac(s), Matt. 8:28 and Mark 5:2.

sides.snippet: When he came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes, two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass by that way.
